support: I laid my hand on her iron side and thought of the mornings, years ago, when I rode up behind her with her smoke drifting back past the carriage windows and the whole village hearing her whistle at Gessen.
At Tarsel the Hollin stands cold in the shed beside the platform, and the climb will never again be made behind her.
WV13-P01.6.note: The author reports the working line plainly and dwells with longing on the retired steam engine and the mornings behind her, which is wistful.

exclusions.A: The pike they swam over is in the terrace now, part of the concrete under the town's feet.

support: When I stand at the deep end now, I still look up for a tower that is gone.
Three generations of Ostley children learned to dive from that tower, and the place where they learned has gone with it.
WV13-P02.5.note: The writer blames no one for the changes but repeatedly mourns the lost tower and tiles, which is regret.
